reason: The passes disagreed (NEEDS_PROOF). Route this report to a human reviewer.

evidence.claim: Repayments/direct transfers to a market are applied to the current pending withdrawal batch (or left idle) instead of the FIFO queue of expired unpaid batches, so a newer batch can be paid before older expired batches.
evidence.support_reason: _getUpdatedState (WildcatMarketBase.sol:406-465) only processes the pending expired batch and the current pending batch; it never iterates _withdrawalData.unpaidBatches. repay (WildcatMarket.sol:202) and plain transfers only call _getUpdatedState, so idle assets are not routed to the FIFO queue. Only repayAndProcessUnpaidWithdrawalBatches (WildcatMarketWithdrawals.sol:283) drains unpaid batches. A new queueWithdrawal creates a fresh pending batch (WildcatMarketWithdrawals.sol:93-99) whose availableLiquidityForPendingBatch can consume the idle assets, paying the newer batch before older expired ones.
preconditions: A withdrawal batch expires unpaid (borrower delinquent on withdrawals).
Borrower repays or transfers assets while no new pending batch exists, so assets sit idle.
A lender queues a new withdrawal, creating a new pending batch that absorbs the idle liquidity.

missing_evidence.item: Demonstration that the newer batch actually receives the idle assets while the older expired batch remains unpaid, and that this violates the stated invariant rather than being consistent with it.
missing_evidence.why: The invariant says assets are only paid to newer batches if the market has sufficient assets to close older batches. The report does not show the older batch could have been closed with the same assets; if the older batch is larger than available liquidity, paying the newer batch may still be consistent with the invariant, so the stated impact is unproven.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: A concrete sequence (amounts, batch sizes, timestamps) shows the older expired batch could be fully closed with the idle assets yet the newer batch is paid first, or the invariant is otherwise concretely broken.
